os_version: Debian 13 (trixie), kernel 6.12.95+deb13-amd64, headless server — Xvfb 1280x800 (X11), no WM, no compositor
app: Per-window pixel capture via XComposite — the X11 implementation of the per-window capture rule (macOS: CGWindowListCreateImage per window; Windows: PrintWindow PW_RENDERFULLCONTENT), demonstrated with a measured verdict flip

stack_detection.method: XCompositeQueryExtension before any capture — the extension's presence is queryable a priori, so a router knows which capture primitive it may use before acting
stack_detection.signature: Composite extension version 0.4 present on stock Xvfb (no compositor needed for manual redirection)

channel_setup: campaign/linux/grabwin.c (~80 lines, plain Xlib + libXcomposite): XCompositeRedirectWindow(CompositeRedirectAutomatic) → force one repaint (XClearArea with exposures) → XCompositeNameWindowPixmap → XGetImage on the pixmap; plus a root-window XGetImage of the same rect as the naive-screen-crop comparator. Analysis in campaign/linux/xcomp-analyze.mjs (PPM→PNG, pixel divergence, guard content-energy on both captures). Setup: Mousepad (800x600) holding two sentinel text lines, FeatherPad (700x500) raised on top covering ~3/4 of it.

t6_pictorial.detail: The two captures of the SAME window rect diverge on 14.2% of pixels: the window-surface capture shows Mousepad's true, complete content (both sentinel lines — including the region occluded on screen), while the screen crop shows FeatherPad's menubar/toolbar/statusbar painted over it. Artifacts kept side by side (xcomp-mousepad-window.png vs xcomp-mousepad-screen.png).

measurements.notes: THE VERDICT FLIP, MEASURED: content-energy of the screen crop = 0.042 — ABOVE the 0.03 guard threshold — vs 0.021 for the window's own surface. A router spot-checking this window's structure-empty region through a screen crop would read the OVERLAPPING window's ink, cross the decision boundary, and file a false '[unverified: pixels show content]' report against the window below. The macOS finding showed the same failure through transparency (129x energy inflation); this shows it through plain occlusion (2x, but straddling the threshold, which is what matters). Same rule, third OS, now implemented on all three: THE PIXEL SPOT-CHECK MUST READ A PER-WINDOW SURFACE, NEVER A SCREEN CROP. Two X11-specific facts worth recording: (1) stock Xvfb ships Composite 0.4 and a client may redirect a single window manually — no compositing window manager required, so the primitive is available even on bare sessions; (2) the redirected surface holds the window's full content INCLUDING occluded regions (like PrintWindow with PW_RENDERFULLCONTENT), so per-window capture is not merely correct, it is strictly more informative than the screen. Latency: one redirect+repaint+read cycle ~600 ms in this implementation (dominated by the deliberate settle sleep; the X round-trips themselves are milliseconds).

runtime_verification.method: Both captures converted to PNG and inspected; sentinel text lines placed in the occluded window beforehand so truth is known by construction; pixel-divergence and guard energies computed by campaign/linux/xcomp-analyze.mjs.
runtime_verification.agreement: Window-surface capture = the window's true content, byte-verifiable against what was typed; screen crop = the composited screen at that rect. The 14.2% divergence is exactly the occluded area painted by the covering window.

permissions_required: None (any X client may redirect and read a window on its own display; no root, no compositor)
